# Project instructions

## Project context

- This is a Unity 6 project using C#. The exact editor version is in [ProjectVersion.txt](../ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt).
- [Mirror](../Assets/Mirror/version.txt) is the installed networking framework.
- [FizzySteamworks](../Assets/Mirror/Transports/FizzySteamworks/README.md) is installed as a Mirror transport for Steam networking.
- Steamworks.NET provides Steamworks API bindings and is installed through the Unity Package Manager Git dependency in [manifest.json](../Packages/manifest.json); its resolved revision is in [packages-lock.json](../Packages/packages-lock.json).
- The game is 2.5D: environments are 3D, while characters use 2D world sprites. The local player's first-person sprites belong to a UI canvas; other players see that character's world sprites.
- [steam_appid.txt](../steam_appid.txt) contains Spacewar's temporary App ID `480` for development. Use the project's own App ID for release; standalone Steam playtests need the file beside the executable.

## Working with the project

- For Steam multiplayer, use the existing Mirror, FizzySteamworks, and Steamworks.NET stack by default. Do not replace these libraries or add alternative networking or Steam packages without the user's approval.
- Before making networking changes, inspect the relevant scripts, scenes, prefabs, NetworkManager, transport assignment, and Steam initialization. Installed packages do not imply that these are configured or working.
- Check the installed package versions and the FizzySteamworks README when choosing APIs or explaining setup. Describe any required Unity Inspector, Steam client, and testing steps, and distinguish unverified behavior from verified results.
- Prefer project code over edits to third-party Mirror or FizzySteamworks sources unless those edits are necessary. Preserve Unity `.meta` files, GUIDs, and serialized references when moving or renaming assets.

## Player foundation

- [NetworkPlayer.prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/NetworkPlayer.prefab) separates owner-only camera/UI from remote world sprites through [PlayerPresentation](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerPresentation.cs). World sprites animate through SpriteRenderer, not Animator.
- [PlayerMovement](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerMovement.cs) uses a CharacterController and the Vector2 `Player/Movement` input action with WASD and a Shift sprint (see Player HUD, health and stamina). Only Mirror's local player reads input; its root transform uses client-to-server synchronization for this basic prototype, not server-validated movement.
- [SampleScene](../Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity) contains [SteamNetworkManager](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamNetworkManager.cs) (a Mirror NetworkManager), NetworkManagerHUD, and FizzySteamworks (SteamSockets). The player prefab is assigned for automatic spawning, with six connections total (host plus five guests). No separate scene camera/audio listener is present.
- [PlayerLook](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerLook.cs) uses the existing Vector2 `Player/Look` pointer-delta binding from the Keyboard&Mouse group, cloned for the local player only. Mouse sensitivity is degrees per pixel (no deltaTime multiplier). Horizontal look rotates the networked player root before movement/interaction; pitch stays on the owner's camera and is limited to +/-85 degrees by default. Existing PlayerVision synchronization picks up camera yaw.
- Mouse capture starts on local spawn. Escape toggles capture for HUD access; focus loss releases it until Escape is pressed again. Steam Overlay temporarily releases capture and pauses look; returning to gameplay discards the first frame of mouse motion. Disabling or despawning the local player releases the cursor.
- [PlayerSpawnPoints](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerSpawnPoints.cs) on the scene's SpawnPoints parent registers its active direct children as Mirror start positions when enabled and unregisters them when disabled. Six children are provided, selected in round-robin order. Add/move spawn children in the Editor before starting a session.
- [Player tests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/NetworkPlayerTests.cs) run in the Unity Test Runner's PlayMode with no active NetworkManager. They use an in-memory host connection, not Steam, to check prefab wiring, WASD/diagonal movement, and owner/remote visibility.

## Player HUD, health and stamina

- [PlayerHealth](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerHealth.cs) on NetworkPlayer has six health, synchronized by server-to-client SyncVars. Server gameplay calls `TakeDamage(positiveAmount)` and `Heal(positiveAmount)`; values clamp to 0..6. There is no client damage Command, automatic death, or automatic healing. New player spawns start at six; the persistent HUD does not persist health across respawns.
- [PlayerHud](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerHud.cs) is a separate Screen Space Overlay [prefab](../Assets/PREFABS/PlayerHud.prefab), placed as a root in SampleScene, not inside NetworkPlayer. It persists via DontDestroyOnLoad, rejects duplicates, binds only to NetworkClient.localPlayer, and hides its panels while no local player exists. Disabling/re-enabling, player replacement and reconnects rebind the UI. Add future local player readouts to this HUD rather than to the player prefab.
- Assign Full Heart, Half Heart and Empty Heart on the HUD component in its prefab; heart slots are left-to-right, two health each (5 = full/full/half, 4 = full/full/empty). Unassigned heart sprites intentionally render nothing. Assign a background Sprite on HealthPanel's Image, set its tint to white for original artwork, and adjust size/anchors as desired. UI Images do not intercept clicks. The existing first-person canvas remains separate and unchanged.
- [PlayerStamina](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerStamina.cs) on NetworkPlayer has 100 maximum stamina in client-to-server SyncVars: the owning client simulates it (like movement) and Mirror relays it to everyone; it is not server-validated. Sprint drains 15/s, regeneration is 10/s after a 0.8 s delay since the last use, and reaching 0 locks every stamina action until 30% refills. Future owner actions (e.g. attacks) call `TryUseStamina(amount)`, which returns false while exhausted.
- `Player/Sprint` is a Button bound to `<Keyboard>/shift` (either Shift). [PlayerMovement](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerMovement.cs) sprints at **Sprint Multiplier** (1.5x) only while Shift is held, movement input exists, stamina allows it, and the player actually moves; standing still with Shift never drains. PlayerVision publishes Run while sprinting when the CharacterDefinition's Run frames are ready, otherwise Walk.
- The HUD's StaminaPanel (background sprite) holds StaminaFill, a Filled/Horizontal/Left Image whose fill amount follows the local player's stamina. Below **Low Stamina Fraction** (30%; exactly 30% does not blink), without complete depletion, only the fill's alpha blinks at **Blinks Per Second** down to **Blink Minimum Alpha**. After complete depletion (`PlayerStamina.IsExhausted`), the whole bar (panel background and fill) blinks until stamina recovers to the 30% threshold, then the background alpha is restored. Filled Images need a sprite assigned.
- [PlayerSprintFov](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerSprintFov.cs) on PlayerCamera eases the owner's FOV out by **FOV Increase** (6 degrees) at **Transition Speed** while sprinting and removes only its own offset afterwards, coordinating with PlayerFearEffects so panic shudder restoration stays correct. NetworkPlayerTests cover Shift sprint speed/drain, regen delay, exhaustion lockout, sync and FOV.
- [PlayMode tests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/PlayerHudTests.cs) cover all health values, stamina fill/blink, owner-only binding, clamping, generated SyncVar serialization, persistence, duplicate prevention, respawn and reconnect. [EditMode tests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/PlayerHudSceneTests.cs) check scene/prefab wiring. These use an in-memory Mirror host, not live Steam.

## Character sprites

- [CharacterDefinition](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/CharacterDefinition.cs) stores Idle, Walk, Run, Attack, and Dead with per-state **Assignment Mode** and **Frames Per Second**. Create assets with **Create > Capstone > Character Definition**. [PlayerCharacter.asset](../Assets/SPRITES/PlayerCharacter.asset) is assigned to the player prefab but needs generated or manually assigned sprite frames.
- **Automatic** is the default and preserves existing definitions. Assign a dedicated PNG per state, set its grid cell size, Pixels Per Unit, and FPS, then click **Slice [State] Sheet & Assign Frames**. [The importer](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/Editor/CharacterSheetImporter.cs) reads every grid cell left-to-right, top-to-bottom and splits the sequence equally in **West, South, East, North** order. Sixteen cells produce four frames per direction. Directional counts must be multiples of four; Dead uses all cells without directions. Sheet dimensions must divide exactly by the cell size; transparent cells count.
- **Manual** provides an editable **Frames Per Direction**, shared by West/South/East/North for that state, and individual Sprite slots. Dead instead has one **Frame Count**. In the PNG Inspector, set Texture Type to Sprite (2D and UI), Sprite Mode to Multiple, Apply, then slice and Apply in Unity's Sprite Editor. Drag the sprite sub-assets into the definition's slots in playback order. The optional sheet provides an **Open Sprite Editor for Manual Slicing** shortcut; manual playback does not require a sheet or generated-grid settings. All frame slots and a positive FPS are required.
- Switching to Manual retains existing frames. Changing the count preserves the leading frames of each direction separately; shrinking drops trailing frames and growing adds empty slots. Switching back to Automatic requires regeneration and overwrites manual assignments. Automatic slicing modifies shared PNG settings, so do not share sheets with incompatible grids/PPU. Automatic frames must be regenerated after changing the sheet/grid/PPU; FPS changes never require regeneration.
- `WorldView` is the visibility root controlled by [PlayerPresentation](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerPresentation.cs); its child `WorldSprites` carries the SpriteRenderer. [PlayerVision](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerVision.cs) on the player root holds both the CharacterDefinition and WorldSprites references and writes the selected frame to `SpriteRenderer.sprite`. Neither WorldView nor WorldSprites needs its own CharacterDefinition component.
- [PlayerVision](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerVision.cs) sends the owner's camera yaw and animation state through Mirror. Each client chooses remote artwork relative to its own player's camera yaw: same facing = North/back, opposite = South/front, observed facing toward viewer's right = East, left = West. Pitch is ignored.
- Only the child WorldSprites transform billboards locally toward the observing camera, upright and without changing the networked player root. Do not network billboard rotations or use a remote player's inactive camera as the observer.
- Idle/Walk follow actual horizontal movement automatically. Future owner gameplay can call `SetAnimationState(Run/Attack/Dead)` and `ResumeMovementAnimation()`. Idle/Walk/Run loop; Attack/Dead hold their last frame. Explicitly setting a state restarts its animation. Run speed, combat, and death controls remain deferred.
- [EditMode character tests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/CharacterDefinitionTests.cs) verify real PNG slicing, stable generated sprite references, FPS playback, dead sequences, and viewer-relative direction math. The PlayMode player tests also verify automatic Idle/Walk states, owner camera/state Commands, SyncVar serialization, and local-only sprite/billboard changes.

## Steam playtests and invites

- [SteamSession](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamSession.cs) initializes Steam before the transport, pumps callbacks, and stops networking before shutting down Steam. Initialization failures disable the HUD and transport and show an error. Steam must be running with the testing account logged in.
- Use the HUD's **Host (Server + Client)** to host. Guests can enter the host's SteamID64 in the HUD and click **Client**. The scene displays the local SteamID64. FizzySteamworks uses Steam IDs, not localhost/IP addresses; test guests with separate Steam accounts.
- [PlayerInteraction](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerInteraction.cs) reads the owner-only Button `Player/Use` action (E). It raycasts from the local camera forward, up to 3.5 units; solid obstacles block it. [SteamInviteInteractable](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamInviteInteractable.cs) can be attached to an object with a non-trigger collider (including a child collider). A placeholder SteamInviteTerminal is already in SampleScene.
- Hosting creates a friends-only Steam matchmaking lobby for invitations/discovery only; the lobby remains the playable SampleScene, not a waiting-room scene. [SteamNetworkManager](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/SteamNetworkManager.cs) shares the lobby ID over a Mirror NetworkMessage with all clients, including manually connected guests. E opens `ActivateGameOverlayInviteDialog(lobbyId)` for actual play invitations. The lobby stores a project marker (Spacewar is shared by unrelated games) and the host SteamID64. Accepting `GameLobbyJoinRequested_t` enters the lobby, validates its metadata/owner, and starts the FizzySteamworks client automatically.
- SteamSession publishes the `connect` rich-presence key for Join Game and still handles `GameRichPresenceJoinRequested_t`, launch `+connect`, and launch `+connect_lobby`. Disconnect before accepting an invite when already hosting/connected. Leaving clears presence and lobby membership; the host closes the lobby and removes its address. Host migration is not supported. Lobby/API errors are logged; E can be retried after asynchronous lobby creation/entry completes.
- Enable Steam Overlay and test invitation UI in a standalone build; it may be unavailable in the Unity Editor. Put the temporary `steam_appid.txt` (480) beside the executable for local development builds. Replace the App ID for release. Movement and interaction pause while Steam Overlay is active.
- With Spacewar's App ID, both testers should already have this project's build running before accepting an invite. Steam cannot reliably cold-launch this custom executable through Spacewar's app configuration; cold-launch invitations need the project's own Steam app configured for distribution.
- [Steam scene tests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/SteamSceneTests.cs) check scene/prefab/input wiring and invite-address validation. PlayMode tests cover spawn registration and owner-only, range-limited, obstruction-aware E interaction. These do not prove live Steam connectivity or overlay behavior; verify those using separate Steam accounts.

## Local camera and endless-night atmosphere

- The player prefab's Camera has a **Far Clip Plane** (40 units originally; user-tuned) and post-processing/depth enabled. Adjust Far Clip Plane on the prefab; no script overwrites it. On NetworkPlayer > PlayerCamera, [PlayerCameraEffects](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerCameraEffects.cs) exposes **World pixelation** with a Pixelation toggle and **Pixel Height** (270 originally; user-tuned). Lower values (e.g. 135) make larger pixels; higher values (e.g. 540) make finer pixels, capped at the camera's output resolution. Changes apply immediately; the horizontal resolution follows the camera's aspect ratio. This quantizes the world image, not mesh geometry, and leaves Screen Space Overlay UI crisp.
- [NightVisionRendererFeature](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NightVisionRendererFeature.cs) is installed on both PC and Mobile URP renderer assets. It uses Unity 6 RenderGraph and requires an intermediate color texture. Only enabled Game cameras carrying PlayerCameraEffects receive the custom passes; remote cameras remain inactive through PlayerPresentation. Fog runs before post-processing; pixelation runs after it. Keep first-person HUD/sprites on Screen Space Overlay canvases so UI remains crisp.
- The scene's existing Global Volume uses [SampleSceneProfile](../Assets/Settings/SampleSceneProfile.asset). **Film Grain > Intensity** controls noise strength (0 disables it; originally 0.35, user-tuned), with Response available for brightness sensitivity. Color Adjustments provide the night palette; the dim blue directional moon light was removed from SampleScene in the Enemy Fear commit, so NightVisionTests' moon-light check fails until one is re-added. Scene Lighting uses dark flat ambient light and no daylight skybox.
- **Capstone > Night Fog** in that profile is a true depth-terminated ray march, not Unity's distance-fog switch. [NightFog](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/NightFog.cs) exposes Enabled, Density, Max Distance, Base Height, Height Falloff, Ambient Color, Light Scattering, Anisotropy, and Steps. More steps reduce banding but increase GPU cost. Fog distance is capped by Camera.farClipPlane. Main directional-light shadows produce shafts; up to eight visible point/spot lights contribute unshadowed scattering (local-light shadows/cookies are not simulated). Transparent materials without depth writes use the opaque depth behind them.
- Leave built-in scene Fog disabled to avoid double fog. Pixelation does not lower the cost of rendering geometry; ray marching adds work, so profile on target hardware. [NightVisionTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/NightVisionTests.cs) check asset wiring; [NightVisionRenderTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/NightVisionRenderTests.cs) measure rendered pixel blocks, grain variance, fog attenuation, light scattering/shadows, and crisp overlay UI. The overlay screenshot test requires a non-batch Editor run because batch mode lacks Unity's end-of-frame screenshot stage; other render tests support batch mode.

## Local enemy-spotting panic

- Attach [EnemyFearSource](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/EnemyFearSource.cs) to an enemy root and assign its body Renderer (or let it find the first child Renderer). It works with mesh, skinned-mesh, or sprite renderers. Full Intensity Distance and Max Distance control linear camera-to-renderer-center falloff; Intensity scales the target's maximum effect. SampleScene contains a tall cube named **EnemyFearTest** at `(4, 1.5, -3)` for playtesting.
- [PlayerFearEffects](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Player/PlayerFearEffects.cs) is on the prefab's PlayerCamera. Only the local owner's enabled camera evaluates sources; no panic state is networked and no shared Volume is modified. Visible renderer bounds are sampled at their center and six face centers, inside the camera's frustum/clipping range, with solid-collider line-of-sight checks. This is a sampled visibility approximation, not GPU pixel/occlusion readback. Walls need colliders on the Occlusion Mask; triggers and the owner's/target's colliders are ignored. Use the strongest visible source, not additive stacking. Chasing/proximity without sight is deferred until enemy AI exists.
- Camera controls expose Build Up/Recovery Speed, extra Vignette Strength, Vertical Grain Strength/Line Count/Line Thickness/Film Jitter Speed, and FOV Shudder/Frequency. **Vertical Line Thickness** is a relative width multiplier: 1 restores the original width, 0.5 (the default) halves it, and smaller values make finer scratches without changing line count or panic intensity. Extremely thin scratches may fall below screen resolution. The shader layers dark edges and continuous, full-height vertical film scratches over the default post-processing, after world pixel sampling and before overlay UI. Film Jitter Speed changes the lines between film frames without introducing vertical gaps within a frame. FOV shudder is bounded around the configured FOV and restores on recovery, camera/view disable, or despawn. Set FOV Shudder to zero to disable camera motion.
- [PlayerFearEffectsTests](../Assets/Tests/PlayMode/PlayerFearEffectsTests.cs) cover distance, sight, occlusion, partial visibility, independent cameras, source lifecycle and FOV restoration. NetworkPlayerTests check ownership even when a remote camera is forcibly enabled; NightVisionRenderTests measure edge darkening, vertical scratch structure and unchanged shared grain.

## Street block generator (PCG map blocks)

- Goal: REPO-style procedural streets built from pre-generated outdoor "blocks" connected at their entrances. Only the authoring tool exists; runtime block connection, scene transfer, and networking are deferred. Level code lives in [Assets/SCRIPTS/Level](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level) (`Capstone.Level` asmdef; editor code in `Capstone.Level.Editor`).
- Author blocks in [StreetBlockWorkshop](../Assets/Scenes/StreetBlockWorkshop.unity) or via **GameObject > Capstone > Street Block Generator**. [StreetBlockGenerator](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/StreetBlockGenerator.cs) holds the settings; its inspector offers **Generate**, **New Seed & Generate**, **Clear Generated**, and **Save As Prefab** (to `Prefab Folder`/`Prefab Name`, default `Assets/PREFABS/StreetBlocks`). Saved prefabs are plain copies; keep the workshop object unpacked so it stays regenerable. Generation is deterministic per seed and rebuilds the `Generated/{Floor, Obstacles, Buildings, Walls, Boundaries, Decorations}` children; failed generation keeps the previous result.
- Size is `Size In Tiles` of the floor prefab (default [Path_Road](../Assets/Prefab/Streets%20Object/Path_Road.prefab), 3 x 3 m). Tiles group into grid cells of `Tiles Per Cell`; the size must be a multiple of it. All blocks that connect must use the same cell size. Block origin is the floor center with Y=0 at the floor top.
- Entrances (0-4): Random or Manual sides (West/South/East/North), centered or random cell, at least 2 tiles wide and at most one cell. A clear L-shaped walkway runs from every entrance to the block center; buildings, walls and decorations never overlap it. [StreetBlock](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/StreetBlock.cs) stores entrances (side, cell, width, local center, obstacle) and draws gizmos (green open, red obstructed).
- Buildings are placed along the perimeter facing inward (prefab front = +Z). Everything, including roofs/overhangs measured from renderer and collider bounds, must stay inside the floor; an oversized building/wall/obstacle/decoration aborts generation with an error naming its size and the floor size. Walls follow **Wall Mode**: *Fill Gaps* (default) puts buildings on the edge and fills only the closed-edge gaps they leave; *Wrap Edges* first wraps the whole edge (except entrances) with wall pieces and then sets each side's buildings back behind its deepest wall piece, without overlapping walls. Spans no wall piece fits get invisible `Boundary Height` box colliders. Decorations scatter with spacing; ones that cannot fit are skipped with a warning. Project prefabs had no colliders, so `Add Missing Colliders` adds box colliders (plus a floor collider).
- Obstacles: `Obstacle Count` entrances receive a random prefab containing [EntranceObstacle](../Assets/SCRIPTS/Level/EntranceObstacle.cs) (Requirement Key, Destruction or KeyAndDestruction; `TryUseKey`/`TryDestroy`, `cleared` UnityEvent, optional deactivation). State is local only; it needs Mirror sync and axe/key items later. [PlaceholderBarricade](../Assets/PREFABS/StreetBlocks/PlaceholderBarricade.prefab) (6 m, Key) and [StreetBlock_Sample](../Assets/PREFABS/StreetBlocks/StreetBlock_Sample.prefab) (6x6 tiles) are provided. Small blocks with several wide entrances leave little room for buildings/decorations.
- [StreetBlockGeneratorTests](../Assets/Tests/EditMode/StreetBlockGeneratorTests.cs) check footprint containment, colliders, clear entrances, raycast-sealed edges, determinism, oversized-roof errors, manual sides/obstacles, obstacle requirements, and the real project assets/workshop.
